title: styled-components
description: Create component-scoped styles with tagged template literals, theming, and prop-driven variants.

data.text: styled-components turns CSS written as a tagged template literal into a React component with a generated class name. Styles are colocated with the component, and props can change them at runtime.

data.caption: src/components/Button.tsx

data.text: Transient props (`$tone`) are consumed by the style function and **not** forwarded to the DOM, which avoids React's "unknown prop" warnings. Extending an existing component uses `styled(Button)`.

data.caption: Theme provider and typed theme

data.title: Install and pin a single version
data.code:
npm install styled-components
npm ls styled-components   # multiple copies break the theme context

data.title: Trade-offs to mention
items: Styles are generated at runtime, so there is a small render-time cost and no benefit from static CSS extraction.
Server rendering requires a style sheet to be collected and serialised for the first paint.
In the Next.js App Router it needs a client component and the SWC plugin (`compiler.styledComponents`).
Build-time alternatives (CSS Modules, vanilla-extract, Tailwind, StyleX) avoid the runtime entirely.

rows: Objects or templates, styled + css prop

terms.definition: A template string passed to a function, letting styled-components parse CSS at runtime.
A prop prefixed with $ used for styling and stripped from the DOM element.
A context provider that supplies design tokens to every styled component.
Collecting generated rules during SSR so the initial HTML is styled.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: State the runtime cost honestly and name a build-time alternative you would choose for a new server-rendered app. That shows you are choosing tools, not defending favourites.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: styled-components produces a component per style with generated class names.
Transient props style without leaking attributes to the DOM.
ThemeProvider shares design tokens; multiple library copies break it.
Runtime CSS-in-JS needs extra work for SSR and Server Components.
data.takeaway: The strongest answer compares styled-components with CSS Modules and Tailwind on runtime cost and SSR.
